marks.gloss_en: זכר לדבר, שנאמר: שבעת ימים שאר לא ימצא בבתיכם -- graded by the baraita itself as זכר, not ראיה
ואומר: ויחפש בגדול החל
ואומר: בעת ההיא אחפש את ירושלים בנרות
ואומר: נר ה׳ נשמת אדם חופש כל חדרי בטן (why this fourth verse is needed is asked at 7b.17-18, the previous unit)
because the light of a lamp is good for the search (the basis term is pesachim_4a_al_mi_livdok's, where Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak gives the same reason for searching at night)

אי נימא בחצר — האמר רבא: חצר אינה צריכה בדיקה, מפני שהעורבין מצויין שם: a courtyard needs no search at all, so the baraita cannot be ruling on how to search one (the memra's reason is p_rava_orvin). Unanswered
אלא באכסדרה — האמר רבא: אכסדרה לאורה נבדקת: a portico IS searched by its own light, so the baraita's ban on sunlight cannot be about it. Unanswered; לא צריכא לארובה דבחדר follows
Rava: a courtyard does not require searching
אי לבהדי ארובה — היינו אכסדרה: the place opposite the skylight is the portico case, which Rava says is searched by its light. Unanswered; אלא לצדדין follows
no -- [the sunlight clause] is needed for a skylight in a room

ואבוקה לא? והאמר רבא: ... למה צדיקים דומין בפני שכינה — כנר בפני האבוקה; ואמר רבא: אבוקה להבדלה מצוה מן המובחר (= p_rava_avuka_havdala, the second ground; the format admits one source per objection). Both memrot rank a torch's light above a lamp's, so why should the baraita exclude the torch? Answered four times, by four voices

Rava: what is 'and a brightness is as the light; rays at His side, and there is the hiding of His power' (Chavakuk 3:4)? -- to what are the righteous comparable before the Shekhina? to a lamp before a torch
זה יכול להכניסו לחורין ולסדקין, וזה אינו יכול (= p_rnby_chorin): the lamp can be put into holes and cracks, the torch cannot
זה אורו לפניו, וזה אורו לאחריו (= p_zevid_oro): the lamp's light is before it, the torch's behind it
האי בעית, והאי לא בעית (= p_pappa_beit): with the torch he is afraid, with the lamp he is not
האי משיך נהורא, והאי מיקטף איקטופי (= p_ravina_meshich): the lamp's light is drawn out steadily, the torch's is cut off in flickers
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: this one [the lamp] -- one can put it into holes and cracks; that one [the torch] -- one cannot put it into holes and cracks
upper and lower wall-holes need no bedika
a wine store one draws from needs bedika -- drinking has no fixed measure
one is not obligated to thrust his hand into holes and cracks to check, because of the danger
